description: kind-cluster Renovate config. Two-part commit message convention:
`commitMessagePrefix: chore(all):` (below) overrides with a scope so commits read
'chore(all): update ...' for portfolio consistency. Both are required — the preset
alone produces 'chore: ...' (no scope), and `commitMessagePrefix` alone is treated
as a literal string prefix without semantic-commit grouping.
platformAutomerge is deliberately false: main requires the ci-pass status
check and true can merge in the ~1s window before the check registers (the
registration race). Do NOT flip to true — see CLAUDE.md conventions.

customManagers.description: Update Makefile tool versions via inline renovate comments. Two matchStrings: (1) plain `VAR := value` pins (mermaid-cli, plantuml, puml2drawio, kubectl, cloud-provider-kind, act-ubuntu); (2) `VAR := image:tag[@sha256:digest]` pins (KIND_NODE_IMAGE) where the trailing tag is the version and an optional @sha256 is the digest. The var-name class is [A-Z0-9_]+ so digit-containing names like PUML2DRAWIO_VERSION match (a prior [A-Z_]+ stopped at the digit and silently dropped it). extractVersion/registryUrl/versioning are all optional so cloud-provider-kind's `extractVersion=^v...` and act-ubuntu's `versioning=loose` are honored (a prior matchString lacked extractVersion and silently dropped CLOUD_PROVIDER_KIND_VERSION). matchString (1) excludes the image:tag shape by anchoring currentValue to end-of-line; matchString (2) captures the tag as currentValue and the optional digest as currentDigest, so KIND_NODE_IMAGE's `kindest/node:vX@sha256:...` form has both tag + digest bumped together.
Update shell-script and cloud-init tool versions via inline renovate comments
matchStrings: # renovate: datasource=(?<datasource>\S+) depName=(?<depName>[A-Za-z0-9_./:-]+)( extractVersion=(?<extractVersion>\S+))?( registryUrl=(?<registryUrl>\S+))?( versioning=(?<versioning>\S+))?\s*\n[ \t]*[A-Z0-9_]+=(?<currentValue>\S+)

customManagers.description: Update Dockerfile ARG default values via inline renovate comments

Track the C4-PlantUML library version pinned in the docs/diagrams/*.puml !include URLs so Renovate proposes bumps; the diagrams-check re-render gate in CI validates the bump. The !include is a raw.githubusercontent URL with no inline `# renovate:` comment, so it needs this dedicated manager rather than the comment-driven ones above.

packageRules.description: Wait 3 days before automerging major updates

Diagram-renderer bumps need a manual PNG regen. A C4-PlantUML or plantuml/plantuml bump that changes the render fails the diagrams-check gate, so the PR cannot auto-merge and must be finished by hand (`make diagrams` + commit the regenerated PNGs on the branch). Disable automerge and add a distinct label so it is not mistaken for a stuck routine bump. See CLAUDE.md 'Diagram renderer bumps' runbook.

Cilium bumps carry a COUPLED, deliberately un-tracked pin. CILIUM_GATEWAY_API_VERSION in scripts/kind-cilium-cluster.sh is the Gateway API CRD channel that Cilium's minor REQUIRES; it is not Renovate-tracked because it must follow Cilium, not latest. A CILIUM_VERSION-only bump therefore ships a HALF upgrade that no PR check can catch: gateway-cilium.yml has no pull_request trigger (push-to-main + cron + dispatch only) and ci.yml's e2e job is tag-gated, so nothing on a PR ever stands up the Cilium cluster. Observed: PR #242 (cilium 1.19.6 -> 1.20.0) merged green and left main RED for 4 consecutive runs, 2026-07-30 .. 2026-08-09 — Cilium 1.20 requires Gateway API >= v1.6.1 (TLSRoute v1alpha2 -> v1), fixed in PR #256. minimumReleaseAge is set here because the repo-wide 3-day buffer matches only `major`, and 1.19 -> 1.20 is a Helm-chart MINOR. Disable automerge + label so a human moves the coupled pin on the SAME branch and proves it with `gh workflow run gateway-cilium.yml --ref <branch>` before merging. See CLAUDE.md 'Cilium bumps' runbook.

Buffer mise tool bumps 3 days at ALL update types. The aqua: backend resolves via github-tags, which sees a tag before the GitHub release artifact (the actual binary) publishes — a fresh minor/patch can otherwise open a PR whose `mise install` 404s in CI. The major-only buffer above does not cover minor/patch, so this adds the buffer for the mise manager specifically.

Point the mise kubectl pin at the SAME source as its three twins. Renovate's mise manager maps any `aqua:<owner>/<repo>` tool to datasource=github-tags packageName=<owner>/<repo> with extractVersion `^v?(?<version>.+)` (lib/modules/manager/mise/backends.ts createAquaToolConfig). For `aqua:kubernetes/kubectl` that is the kubernetes/kubectl STAGING repo, whose tags are `v0.37.1` and `kubernetes-1.37.1` — never `v1.37.1` — so the lookup returns NO update for a 1.x pin, ever. Measured with `renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup` on a tree pinned at 1.37.0 while 1.37.1 was 9 days old: without this rule `updates: []`; with it 1.37.0 -> 1.37.1 on branch renovate/kubectl alongside the Makefile, images/Dockerfile and vm/cloud-init.yaml pins. Consequence before this rule: the grouped kubectl PR carried 3 of the 4 pins and failed check-toolchain-alignment until a human pushed the .mise.toml half as a separate commit (observed on #274, commit 937b9fc, and #324, commit 0dc257d; #100 and #228 were human-authored repair PRs for the same drift). overridePackageName redirects the lookup to kubernetes/kubernetes (the repo the custom.regex twins track) and is the load-bearing half; extractVersion is the stricter `v`-only form of the manager default and is not required for the lookup to work. GROUPING: the kubectl group rule below uses matchPackageNames, which tests packageName, so the mise pin is grouped because its OVERRIDDEN packageName `kubernetes/kubernetes` is in that list — do not remove `kubernetes/kubernetes` from it. The `aqua:kubernetes/kubectl` entry there matches nothing.

Strip jq's `jq-` tag prefix. jqlang/jq tags are `jq-1.8.2`; the mise manager's auto extractVersion `^v?(?<version>.+)` leaves the prefix, so the pin resolves to currentVersion `jq-1.8.1` and no update is ever proposed. Same root cause as the kubectl rule above (generic aqua lookup vs. a non-`v` tag scheme). Measured with `renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup` on a tree pinned at 1.8.1: without this rule `updates: []`; with it 1.8.1 -> 1.8.2. Must be keyed on matchDepNames: the same rule keyed on matchPackageNames `aqua:jqlang/jq` never matches (packageName is `jqlang/jq`) and leaves `updates: []`. That is a likely explanation for the 2026-06-29 finding that a packageRule extractVersion does not override the mise manager's value; what was run then is not recorded.

NOTE (2026-10-02): the release-age mismatch described below was not the whole story — until the kubectl lookup rule above was added, the mise kubectl twin was never proposed at ANY age. This buffer is kept because, for kubectl, both halves now resolve from kubernetes/kubernetes and must become eligible on the same day. The kind group is unified the same way: both its .mise.toml half and its vm/cloud-init.yaml half are github-tags on kubernetes-sigs/kind. Since renovatebot/renovate#43451 (2026-05-19) github-tags takes the GitHub Release's publishedAt when a release exists, so a github-tags half and a github-releases half already reported the same releaseTimestamp (measured for kind v0.33.0 with `renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup`, 44.132.2: 2026-08-26T21:58:46Z on both, although the tag commit is 21:27:15Z). They could still diverge for a tag with no release, or when the releases query fails (github-tags falls back to the tag time, github-releases fails its lookup) — the reason the cloud-init pin was moved to github-tags. Mirror the mise manager's 3-day minimumReleaseAge onto the github-based kubectl (kubernetes/kubernetes) and kind (kubernetes-sigs/kind) pins that check-toolchain-alignment cross-checks against their .mise.toml aqua: twins. Without this, the github-tracked half (Makefile KUBECTL_VERSION, images/Dockerfile ARG, vm/cloud-init.yaml) becomes eligible ~day 0 while its buffered mise twin (aqua:kubernetes/kubectl, aqua:kubernetes-sigs/kind) waits until day 3, so the grouped kubectl/kind PR opens with ONLY the github half and check-toolchain-alignment reddens it for ~3 days every patch (observed: PR #225, kubectl v1.36.2->v1.36.3, 2026-07-23). The group already cannot MERGE before day 3 (the alignment gate blocks the partial state under platformAutomerge:false + required ci-pass), so buffering the github half adds no real merge delay — it only stops opening a doomed-red PR early, and both halves then bump atomically. Does NOT cover kindest/node: the node-image K8s version is a separate axis, not compared by the alignment gate.
Group GitHub Actions into one PR

Disable digest pinning for ALL custom.regex-tracked docker pins. Covers two file groups: (a) Makefile dev tools (MERMAID_CLI_VERSION, PLANTUML_VERSION, PUML2DRAWIO_VERSION, KIND_NODE_IMAGE, ACT_UBUNTU_VERSION) — preventive per /renovate skill's `docker:pinDigests × version-bump` collision class; (b) scripts/*.sh workload-image refs (hashicorp/http-echo, gcr.io/.../hello-app, ghcr.io/.../golang-web, registry) — the shell-script regex captures `IMAGE=foo/bar:${X_VERSION}` constructions which cannot carry an `@sha256:...` digest in the variable's value, so the Pin Dependencies operation kept failing on these (Dependency Dashboard 'Repository Problem: Error updating branch'). Production-runtime docker pins (Dockerfile FROM, k8s/*.yaml image: fields) keep their digest pins via the dockerfile + kubernetes managers respectively.

Keep workload image bumps in sync across k8s/*.yaml and scripts/*.sh — YAML image: field (kubernetes manager) and matching scripts' IMAGE= variable (custom.regex on shell) land in one PR so `kind load docker-image` and `kubectl apply` can't disagree on the tag. matchUpdateTypes scopes the rule to per-package updates only — Renovate's Pin Dependencies operation bundles many unrelated deps into one PR with no single {{depName}} for the template to resolve, which produced a literal `workload-image-depname` branch name and an `Error updating branch: update failure` in the Dependency Dashboard. Letting `pin` fall back to default grouping fixes the collapse.

Keep kubectl in sync across .mise.toml (mise manager) and Makefile KUBECTL_VERSION (custom.regex, used as a Dockerfile --build-arg). The Makefile pin is `# renovate: datasource=github-tags depName=kubernetes/kubernetes`; the mise pin extracts to `aqua:kubernetes/kubectl`. The `kubernetes/kubectl` entry is a defensive alias in case Renovate's docker-tag manager surfaces that depName form for any future Dockerfile reference.

Keep kind in sync across .mise.toml (mise manager), vm/cloud-init.yaml (custom.regex), and the Makefile KIND_NODE_IMAGE pin (kindest/node). The kind binary and its node image are released together per KinD release notes — grouping them lands the coupled bump in one PR instead of two.

Suppress lookups for the local registry image. `make registry` wires containerd to localhost:5001 for in-cluster development; Renovate cannot reach localhost. The tag is templated into the manifest at apply time by `scripts/test-registry.sh` (single source of truth = HELLO_APP_VERSION there, Renovate-tracked via the upstream gcr.io/google-samples/hello-app pin), so the hardcoded tag in `k8s/helloweb-deployment-local.yaml` is just a fallback for direct kubectl apply.
